export.description: Everything as one Excel file — a sheet per domain, with an ID column so the file can be read back in later.

hints.cruises: One row per cruise. Do not change the ID in column A — it is what matches the row back to its record on import. A row without an ID is created as a new cruise.
hints.cruiseStops: One row per port day or sea day. The “Cruise” column points to the “Cruises” sheet through the ID in square brackets — without an ID, the name in front of it counts. Rows without an ID are created as new stops.
hints.lodging: One row per property. Rows without an ID are created as new properties. Stays have their own sheet, because a property can have any number of them.
hints.lodgingStays: One row per stay. The “Lodging” column points to the “Lodging” sheet through the ID in square brackets — without an ID, the name in front of it counts. Rows without an ID are created as new stays. Nights are calculated and cannot be set here.
hints.places: One row per place. Rows without an ID are created as new places. Visits have their own sheet.
hints.placeVisits: One row per visit. The “Place” column points to the “Places” sheet through the ID in square brackets — without an ID, the name in front of it counts.
hints.flights: One row per flight. Do not change the ID in column A — it is what matches the row back to its record on import. Airports travel as IATA codes; changing a code moves the flight. A row without an ID is created as a new flight.

import.title: Excel import
import.description: Read an edited export file back in — also into a different account. Rows carrying an ID from your account update that entry. Rows without an ID, or with an ID from another account, are created; entries that already exist (the same flight on the same day, the same property with the same check-in …) are recognised instead of duplicated. The file is checked first — nothing is written until you confirm.
import.failed: The file could not be read.
import.nothing: The file holds no sheets we recognise.
import.hasErrors: Some rows have problems. Nothing is applied while they are in there.

errors.invalid_coordinates: Latitude or longitude is not a number.
errors.invalid_number: A number in this row is not a number.
errors.invalid_date: A date in this row cannot be read.
errors.too_many_rows: That sheet has too many rows.
errors.visit_needs_place: A new visit has to name a place — the ID in square brackets in the “Place” column.
errors.unknown_place: That place is neither in your account nor on the “Places” sheet.
errors.invalid_rating: A rating has to be between 1 and 5.
errors.unknown_airport: That IATA code is not known.
errors.flight_needs_route: A new flight needs From, To, airline and flight number.
errors.invalid_row: The row is incomplete or holds an invalid value.
errors.ambiguous_place: Several places have that name — please give the ID in square brackets.
errors.stop_needs_cruise: A new stop has to name a cruise — the “Cruise” column.
errors.unknown_cruise: That cruise is neither in your account nor on the “Cruises” sheet.
errors.ambiguous_cruise: Several cruises have that name — please give the ID in square brackets.
errors.stay_needs_lodging: A new stay has to name a property — the “Lodging” column.
errors.unknown_lodging: That property is neither in your account nor on the “Lodging” sheet.
errors.ambiguous_lodging: Several properties have that name — please give the ID in square brackets.

import.modeLabel: What should happen to entries that already exist?

add.label: Add only
add.hint: Creates new entries. Anything already there is left as it is, even where the file says otherwise.

merge.label: Merge
merge.hint: Rows with an ID update the existing entry, rows without one are created. Nothing is deleted.

replace.label: Replace contents
replace.hint: Like merge — and additionally deletes everything the file leaves out.

import.replaceWarningTitle: This deletes entries you cannot see right now
import.replaceWarning: Anything missing from the file will be deleted. Those entries are not in the sheet you opened — they are absent from it. A full backup is taken automatically before anything is written, so the import can be undone.
import.confirmReplace: I understand that {{count}} entries will be deleted
import.backupFailed: The safety backup failed — nothing was changed.
import.emptySheetNote: An empty sheet deletes nothing. To empty a domain, remove its rows one by one.
import.transferNote: The spreadsheet carries entries, not photos, documents or receipts. Trips are not a sheet of their own: an entry is linked to the trip of the same name in the target account, otherwise it stays without a trip. Moving a whole installation, photos and documents included, to another server is what the backup is for; it cannot move a single account into another account.

notes.trip_not_linked: trip not found in this account — imported without a trip
notes.port_not_found: port not in the catalogue — left empty
notes.chain_not_found: chain not in the catalogue — imported without a chain
